item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 051729
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Mon Oct 5 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Rachel, located a few hundred miles west-southwest of the southern
tip of the Baja California Peninsula.

South of Southern Mexico (92E):
A broad area of low pressure located near the Gulf of Tehuantepec is
producing disorganized showers and thunderstorms. Environmental
conditions appear favorable for gradual development, and a tropical
depression is expected to form during the next few days while the
system moves slowly west-northwestward to northwestward. Interests
along the coast of southwestern Mexico should monitor the progress
of this system.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...medium...60 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

$$
Forecaster Cangialosi

item.title: Hurricane Rachel Public Advisory Number 35
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM PDT Mon Oct 05 2026 
000
WTPZ33 KNHC 052032
TCPEP3
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Rachel Advisory Number  35
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
200 PM PDT Mon Oct 05 2026
 
...RACHEL SLIGHTLY BETTER ORGANIZED...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 PM PDT...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...20.3N 117.1W
ABOUT 495 MI...800 KM WSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...90 MPH...150 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 265 DEGREES AT 8 MPH...13 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...973 MB...28.74 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 PM PDT (2100 UTC), the eye of Hurricane Rachel was located
near latitude 20.3 North, longitude 117.1 West. Rachel is moving
toward the west near 8 mph (13 km/h) and a continued westward to
west-northwestward motion is expected for the next several days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 90 mph (150 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Fluctuations in strength are possible over the next couple of 
days, with gradual weakening beginning by the middle part of the 
week.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 40 miles (65 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 140 miles
(220 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 973 mb (28.74 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Rachel will continue to affect the coast
of the Baja California Peninsula for the next couple of days.
These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 PM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Cangialosi

item.title: Hurricane Rachel Forecast Discussion Number 35
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM PDT Mon Oct 05 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 052033
TCDEP3
 
Hurricane Rachel Discussion Number  35
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
200 PM PDT Mon Oct 05 2026
 
The weakening trend of Rachel has paused for now. Satellite images
suggest that the hurricane has become slightly better organized
over the past several hours. The eye of the system is quite large,
well defined and warm, and deep convection remains fairly
symmetric around the center. A blend of the latest satellite
intensity estimates supports nudging the initial intensity up to 80
kt.
 
The hurricane is moving westward at 7 kt steered by a high pressure 
system to the north-northeast of the cyclone. A continued westward 
to west-northwestward motion is expected during the next few days as 
the high pressure system remains the primary steering feature. 
However, by the weekend, the high is expected to weaken as a mid- to 
upper-level trough amplifies near the west coast of the U.S. This 
pattern change should cause Rachel to slow down and then turn 
northeastward by the end of the forecast period. No significant 
changes were made to the previous track forecast, and this one lies 
generally near the middle of the guidance envelope.

Although Rachel appears a little stronger than earlier, no notable 
changes to the intensity forecasts were made. The hurricane is 
expected to gradually weaken as it moves over progressively cooler 
waters and into a much drier airmass. The models have not changed 
much this cycle, and this prediction is in line with the HCCA, 
GDMI, and IVCN aids.
